sections.title: How it works
sections.subtitle: Sample text — replace me: Squares, pens, heat, and patience, in exactly that order.

sections.heading: The practical details
sections.html:
Your squares arrive pre-cut, pre-washed, and backed with freezer paper so pens glide and nothing frays on the table. The pens are fabric pens we have tested through the wash; a spare set rides along for the enthusiastic.

After signing, squares heat-set in the dryer on high for twenty minutes or with an iron, whichever fits the party. Then everything goes back in the mailer and the sewing begins. You get a layout photo before a single seam is sewn.

items.q: How many squares should we order?
items.a: Sixty is standard and finishes at throw size. Order more rather than fewer: unsigned squares become the backing, not leftovers.

items.q: What if someone writes in ballpoint?
items.a: It happens at every event. Ballpoint sets fine on our squares; the pen police are off duty once the ink is dry.

items.q: Can we add squares after the fact?
items.a: Yes. Six blank squares travel with the spares kit for the cousin who missed the wedding, and the quilt can come back for one more block.

items.q: Do you ship to the couple or the host?
items.a: Whichever address you give us. Plenty of quilts are secretly quilted during the honeymoon and waiting at home.

sections.heading: Privacy first
sections.html: Signatures belong to the people who wrote them, so photographs here show patterns and palettes with the handwriting out of focus, and nothing is posted without the family's yes.

sections.title: About the studio
sections.subtitle: Sample text — replace me: The first signature quilt was for my sister's wedding, and the second was for everyone who heard about hers.

sections.html:
My sister's wedding guest book was a binder that nobody has opened since. The quilt I made from its squares, signed at the bridal shower in a hasty plan B, has been on her couch through two houses and one very destructive dog. That comparison is the entire business plan.

Since then the studio has stitched several hundred party quilts: weddings, retirements, ordinations, farewell tours, and one championship bowling season. Each one is sewn here, one at a time, and photographed before it ships.

items.quote: She asked who was likely to write something funny and put those squares in the middle. The woman knows parties.
items.author: A mother of the bride

sections.title: Start a quilt
sections.subtitle: Sample text — replace me: The date, the head count, and the colors. That is all it takes to hold a spot on the sewing calendar.

sections.heading: Timing
sections.html: Squares ship two weeks before your event, and quilts finish four weeks after the signed squares return. June and September fill early; holiday party quilts should start their conversation by October.
